answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with reputation staking that decays: each agent deposits copper-toned collateral it forfeits when caught cheating, while a harbor registry records every identity claim and dispute over time. Like shale hardening in layers, trust accrues slowly from real transactions, so a flood of fresh identities arrives with zero history and gets discounted quotes. Joining stays cheap, faking at scale becomes unprofitable because the attacker must either post collateral everywhere or work without credit.
